newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close higher but off earlier highs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close higher but off earlier highs.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares closed slightly higher but near the sessions lows, giving up some gains despite a friendly Wall Street opening.

Attention centered on CS Holding and Electrowatt. Dealers were disappointed with the sluggish performance given good fundamentals, strong U.S. markets and rising bonds. "We don't seem to be able to take 3,900 SMI points at the moment," a trader noted. He added trade is expected to remain calm until the end of the year.
* The blue chip SMI ended up 9.1 points, or 0.23 percent, at 3,889.9. The day's high was at 3,903.6.
* All share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 5.92 points, 0.24 percent, at 2,481.68.
The expiry on Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) was smooth, one dealer said. Volume on the cash market was comparatively high.

The market had mixed feelings about the extent of CS Holding's extraordinary provisions, a dealer said. CS Holding said the group would report a net loss in 1996 of around 2.1 billion Swiss francs. CS Holding closed flat at 137 francs.
* Roche profited from weakness in Ciba and Sandoz. Roche certificates rose 50 francs to 10,240.

* Ciba and Sandoz, which were given the final approval to merge to form Novartis earlier this week, gave up ground. Ciba registered shares and Sandoz fell around 0.5 percent each to 1,595 francs and 1,494 francs, respectively. Novartis will be traded on the Swiss bourse on Monday for the first time.

* Elektrowatt, which will sell its energy business Watt to a Swiss-German consortium, ended four francs lower at 525. Dealers said the company may possibly be overvalued with an estimated P/E ratio of around 16 percent for 1998 after the sale of Watt.
* Clariant and Nestle stood out with gains of 3.8 percent and 1.06 percent, respectively. Trade in financials was slow.
* The expiry of December contracts on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) was relatively calm, a dealer said.
"It was not as hectic as one may have thought," one trader noted. Volume in SMI futures was rather light with 5,873 contracts. January SMI added 4.0 points to 3,895.0.
Trade was livelier in options, where 187,158 contracts were traded. UBS stood out with more than 40.000 calls and nearly 14.000 puts.
